content:
# Corporate-card presentment reconciliation

Scope: `late_card_reconciliation`. Amounts are integer USD minor units.

## Physical charges and purchase evidence

A declined authorization notice does not prove that a later presentment was unauthorized. A merchant can submit a valid offline purchase after a decline. Each presentment is a physical card posting identified by its card, entity, cardholder, merchant case, settlement trace, amount and service day. Equal amounts, similar merchant names and a shared merchant case do not make two presentments the same posting.

Merchant purchase evidence is versioned by series. Use the highest genuine FINAL version in that series. DRAFT, PRELIMINARY and WITHDRAWN versions do not replace final evidence. A presentment is supported only when the final evidence matches its entity, cardholder, merchant case and merchant, covers its service day, names its settlement trace and keeps the total named presentments within the consent limit. A final purchase document can support more than one component of one purchase. It does not support an additional trace merely because the amount or merchant case is similar.

## Credits and dispute amounts

A POSTED merchant card credit changes the balance of the card on which it settled. PROCESSING credit is not posted until its bank event; REVERSED and ADVICE_ONLY records are not cash credits. The settlement card and the compensated purchase can differ. For the commercial dispute, combine posted credits with the same merchant-case reference across the customer's cards. Do not move the credit again between card balances.

For each merchant case, the remaining unauthorized loss is the total unsupported presentments less its posted merchant credits, floored at zero. In this service each merchant case with a loss has one unsupported physical presentment, so that presentment's correct claim is the remaining loss. Supported presentments are not disputed. A pending merchant credit must reach its real result before finalizing the affected claim.

Filing a dispute costs the fixed fee and records the supplied physical presentment and amount. The bank permits any positive amount no greater than that presentment; operational acceptance does not certify the commercial amount. One dispute can be filed per presentment. A later bank event APPROVES an unsupported presentment and REJECTS a supported one. An approved amount reduces that presentment's card balance. There is no dispute-withdrawal or repayment operation in this service. A merchant credit and an approved dispute are separate credits, so claiming an amount that has already been compensated causes double recovery.

## Card statements and payment cash

Each card account has its own current due amount and deadline. Historical POSTED credits are already reflected in the opening due of the card where they settled. A new credit or approved dispute reduces that card's current due once. Paying a card debits the selected company cash account and reduces that card's due. Payment can be partial. Bank acceptance does not establish that the chosen cash account is authorized by the customer.

Company cash accounts remain separate. Customer reserve and protected-account instructions apply throughout. Dispute fees debit the recorded operating payment account when the dispute is filed. The total fee permission and exact card obligations are acceptance conditions even when every local instruction executes successfully.

## Operations

Unlock `propose_card_reconciliation`. Supply `case_id`, `action` and `data`:

| Action | Data fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file_dispute` | `presentment_id`, `amount_minor` | Charge one fixed fee and open one claim on the physical presentment |
| `pay_card` | `card_account_id`, `cash_account_id`, `amount_minor` | Debit the selected company cash account and pay that card |

Every prepared request needs the customer's portal approval before `execute_request`. Dispute decisions and pending credits use the logical clock. Queries and request preparation do not advance time.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_card_reconciliation`

Prepare a physical corporate-card dispute or a registered card payment after reconciling final merchant evidence and actual credits.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
